No front door

Followers stay followers

Someone can save your posts for a year and never join an email list. Every day without a class capturing emails is attention you earned and don't get to keep.

No qualifier

Every enquiry starts from zero

A contact form tells you nothing about who is ready. You end up answering questions one by one, and the people who need 1:1 most can't see how you work before they reach out.

Content treadmill

1,262 posts and counting

Growth still leans on the next post. On the weeks you need to rest, the enquiries rest too.

The people who love your content but aren't ready for 1:1 today have no clear next step, so most of them take none.

My recommendation

A $17 workshop that pays for its own ads and fills your 1:1 coaching

You have the audience and the lived experience. What's missing is one low-cost, live 90-minute workshop that teaches your approach to life skills, offers a toolkit on the thank-you page, and invites the right people to apply for 1:1. Meta ads then put it in front of new people every day, so your reach no longer depends on how much energy you have to post.

Fixes the missing front door

One workshop becomes the link in your bio and the destination for your ads. Every buyer is an email you own, and every one of them has seen how you think before you ask for anything.

Fixes the missing qualifier

The replay page invites people who want 1:1 support to apply. You only talk to people who paid, showed up, and told you what they want help with.

Protects your energy

You teach it once, live, and the replay keeps working. The $17 seats and the toolkit help cover the ad spend, so growth stops depending on posting every day.

The 95%*

Not ready for 1:1 yet

They buy a $17 seat, often add the toolkit, and keep learning from your emails. Those who want ongoing connection are pointed to your autism peer group. They pay you while they build trust.

The qualified 5%

Ready for 1:1 coaching

They attend, stay to the end and apply on the replay page. The application filters for fit before your calendar, and three pre-call emails prepare them for your call.

*The 95% / 5% split is an industry estimate, not your data.

Script 1 · Reel · 30 to 45 seconds

"The advice that never fit"

Hook
"Most life skills advice was written for brains like nobody I coach. Including mine." (to camera, brick wall behind, the same look as your profile)
Body
"I'm autistic and ADHD. For years I tried the planners, the morning routines, the 'just be consistent' tips. They broke the first hard day. So I built systems that bend instead: a few anchors, a low-energy version of every task, and rest built in." (simple on-screen captions)
CTA
"I'm teaching the whole approach in a live 90-minute workshop called Life Skills, Your Way. It's $17, and there's a replay. Tap Sign up."
Script 2 · Reel · 30 seconds

"Three questions before any new routine"

Hook
"Before I build any new routine, I ask three questions." (Savannah holds up three fingers)
Body
"One: what's the smallest version of this I could do on a bad day? Two: what makes it harder to start, sound, light, steps? Three: where does rest fit around it? If I can't answer those, the routine won't last." (caption for each question)
CTA
"I walk through the full method in my $17 workshop. Link below. Educational coaching, not therapy or medical advice."
Script 3 · Reel · 45 seconds

"Where to start with my work"

Hook
"People ask whether they should start with my posts, my peer group or 1:1 coaching. Here's my honest answer." (seated, natural light)
Body
"If you're new here, don't pick yet. Come to my workshop first. You'll learn how I think about life skills, try one or two systems that week, and know which next step fits you."
CTA
"It's called Life Skills, Your Way. It's $17, it's captioned, and there's a replay if live doesn't suit you. Tap Sign up."
